query: Should the unit of analysis be per specimen, per ordered test, or per reported result, and how will multi-analyte panels and multiplex results be counted operationally?

response.query: Should the unit of analysis be per specimen, per ordered test, or per reported result, and how will multi-analyte panels and multiplex results be counted operationally?
response.answer: The unit of analysis is per specimen for immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization. Multi-analyte panels and multiplex results are counted as one unit per specimen.

results.content:
Title: How to design an archetype to report a combination of different lab test results - Clinical - openEHR
# How to design an archetype to report a combination of different lab test results. I want to design an archetype which provides an evaluation to the user based on several lab test results. Use **Laboratory test result** archetype and its ‘Test result’ attribute will contain the openEHR-EHR-CLUSTER.laboratory\_test\_analyte.v1. Since in my scenario it contains multiple lab test results, openEHR-EHR-CLUSTER.laboratory\_test\_analyte.v1 will be repeated inside Laboratory test result\*. Use **Laboratory test result** archetype and its ‘Test result’ attribute will contain the openEHR-EHR-CLUSTER.laboratory\_test\_analyte.v1. But it will use **only one instance** of openEHR-EHR-CLUSTER.laboratory\_test\_analyte.v1. That instance will contain all the lab test results. Almost certainly option 1 and carry your summary in the laboratory test. Although I’d consider making a separate instance of the OBSERVATION.laboratory\_test\_result per specimen type. The Analyt result attribute accepts data belongs to any data type . So I thought to add 4 Quantity type attributes to represent the above test results. Typically i would expect the urine tests and bood results to be ordered and reported separately. Then we can use a CLUSTER to group analyte results into batteries/panels (see LOINC 24357-6 Urinalysis macro (dipstick) panel - Urine). In the vast majority of lab use-cases, the Lab test observation works fine as a container but we do have a specific archetype for Urinalysis (which is usually a bedside test, not lab reported). ### Observation Archetype: Urinalysis. results.title: BioPlex 2200 ANA Screen with MDSS — Bio-Rad
results.content: # BioPlex 2200 ANA Screen with MDSS. The BioPlex 2200 ANA Screen uses multiplex technology to generate up to 14 individual results per test: a composite ANA screen result plus up to 13 ANA analyte results. BioPlex 2200 ANA Screen Panel. With the fully automated BioPlex 2200 System, the BioPlex 2200 ANA Screen can provide up to 1,400 individual results per hour and eliminates separate follow-up testing to help clinical laboratories streamline workflow, automate testing processes, and manage ANA workloads better. #### Each BioPlex 2200 ANA Screen reagent pack uses multiplex technology to deliver up to 14 results:. † RNP (A and 68) is reported as a composite results in the U.S. Learn more about the BioPlex 2200 ANA Screen. Multiplexing takes full automation to the next level by allowing labs to complete ANA screening and follow-up testing in one step. ANA testing using IFA or other traditional EIA methods requires initial screening and multiple follow-up tests. In comparison, multiplexed ANA panels enable labs to use a single test to complete ANA screening and follow-up testing. Labs can expand in-house ANA testing menus and reduce send-out testing costs, all while using fewer reagents, calibrators, controls, and consumable supplies. By conducting an ANA screen and follow-up testing in a single step, labs can dramatically enhance result turnaround time and provide better patient care.
